title: Musk’s Terafab faces trademark dispute before making a single chip
author: Xebec
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Elon Musk’s planned Terafab chip factory has encountered a trademark fight before producing its first semiconductor. Tesla, SpaceX and SpaceXAI sued Illinois nanotechnology company TERA-print in federal court in Texas on September 15, seeking a declaration that the Terafab name does not infringe TERA-print’s Tera-Fab mark.

The dispute began after Tesla applied for Terafab trademarks in May. TERA-print sent a cease-and-desist letter, arguing that the similar names could confuse customers. The smaller company says it has used Tera-Fab for more than a decade and received a federal trademark registration in 2021. Its product is a desktop lithography system used in research, including bioengineering. TERA-print

Musk’s companies argue that the businesses operate in different markets. Their planned factory would manufacture, package and test advanced logic and memory chips, while TERA-print sells laboratory equipment. In their complaint, they say buyers would have no reason to think the Texas plant was connected to TERA-print. The lawsuit asks a judge to settle that question before the project moves further under the Terafab name. Reuters

TERA-print rejects that distinction. It says its technology and business extend into semiconductor fabrication and artificial intelligence, making confusion plausible. The company also says it was discussing a settlement with Tesla as recently as September 2 and intends to defend its trademark in court. These are competing claims, and the court has not decided whether either side has the stronger right to the name. TERA-print

The stakes go beyond a label. Terafab is intended to supply chips for Tesla’s robots and vehicles and SpaceX’s proposed space-based computing systems. A name change could complicate branding, although the case itself does not establish that chip production will be delayed. For now, the project’s first public legal contest concerns what its factory can be called, rather than what it can make. Reuters
